title: The wreath conjecture for decompositions of uniform subsets
statement: Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let a **wreath** be the collection of intervals obtained from a cyclic permutation of $[n]$ by choosing a $k$-element interval and then successively choosing the interval starting immediately after the end of the preceding one, continuing until the initial interval is reached. Thus a wreath contains $\operatorname{lcm}(n,k)/k$ intervals and goes around the cycle $\operatorname{lcm}(n,k)/n$ times. **The wreath conjecture.** The family of all $k$-element subsets of $[n]$ can be decomposed into disjoint wreaths. This is an old and difficult problem related to the Baranyai theorem; the source mentions related earlier results and open problems, but does not indicate a resolution of this conjecture.
source_name: Gyula O. H. Katona and Gyula Y. Katona, “Towards a Baranyai theorem with additional condition”, arXiv:2312.09134 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.09134

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2023). “Finally let us mention that paper contains some related earlier results and open problems.”
